choices.background: The kettle. The answer she reaches for before she has heard mine.
She kept the lantern burning. I noticed from halfway down the path.
Cold. Angry. Two things. She does know the difference.
I said they were perfect. It was easier than saying they hurt.
I needed my leaving to feel real to her.
She meant it then. I can hear that now.
She watched the door all night. Why did it stay shut?
I read the note again and again. The words would not stay put.
I made it halfway. That has to count for something.
Yes. No soft edge around it. Just yes.
She wants to ask. I can see her trying not to fill the silence.
The list again. How do I make her hear me without turning this into an errand?
I am not sure I know any more. The words are somewhere; I cannot reach them yet.
Milk had an answer. She needed me to hear the question underneath it.
I do not have to be fixed before I sit beside her.
She brought my cup back. She remembered which one was mine.
I was angry. I still wanted her there.
May I take it? Such a small question to ask after all this.
Not yet. I am not ready for the threshold.
